0.original: The veteran Radiant wishes to share his gratitude.

24.original: Speak with Y'shtola at the High Crucible of Al-Kimiya.

25.original: Speak with Y'shtola at Sharlayan's aetheryte plaza and have her accompany you.

26.original: Speak with Montichaigne while Y'shtola is accompanying you.

27.original: Speak with the House Leveilleur butler while Y'shtola is accompanying you.

28.original: Accompany Y'shtola to the Baldesion Annex and speak with her.

48.original: Vrtra is warming to his role as satrap. Clearly all those years behind the curtain were not spent napping.

49.original: Thank you for putting forth Khalzahl's name. Those whose lives he enriched will take comfort in seeing his legacy honored.

50.original: You will forgive me for not speaking sooner, but I bear a message from Archon Y'shtola. She asks that you meet her at the High Crucible at your earliest convenience.

52.original: Y'shtola must have finished her study of the voidgate. Shall we hear what she has to say, then?

54.original: I thought the satrap would be too busy setting up the foundation...?

55.original: My clerks have been the well-oiled cogs of this administration since before Ahewann assumed the office. They understand what needs to be done.

56.original: And I am curious to learn what conclusions your Archon has reached concerning the gate's unique construction.

57.original: As you wish. Allow me to lead the way, Your Excellency.

58.original: You can find your way to the High Crucible, I trust? I must rejoin my unit and assist with bringing the city's orphans under our care.

59.original: For one who claims it is “too late” to save his sister, Vrtra seems awfully interested in whatever revelations Y'shtola might have to share.

60.original: Shall we hear what your scholarly comrade has to say?

62.original: If we're to enter Noumenon's restricted archives with a minimum of fuss, then we must secure the permission of the Forum.

63.original: First, however, we shall need to enlist the cooperation of a member to broach the matter on our behalf. Who do you think might be inclined to assist us?

74.original: He did come to G'raha's defense during the inquiry, after all.

75.original: 'Tis settled. Let us head to Phenomenon and see if he's willing to help us once more.

76.original: Y'shtola is now accompanying you. Keep her at your side in order to proceed with quest objectives.

77.original: You can leave Y'shtola behind by entering a different area, or by speaking with her and selecting the option to part ways.

78.original: If you wish to have Y'shtola accompany you again, return and speak with her at the original location.

79.original: I apprenticed to Master Matoya at the age of seven, and labored under her tutelage for a full decade. I never had the chance to attend the Studium...

80.original: Neither did Thancred, as I recall. Soon after Master Louisoix took him in off the streets, he was put in the care of another Archon. His was a rigorous and practical education in the arts of espionage and survival.

81.original: I sometimes wonder what my life might have been like had I pursued studies here instead...

83.original: Tea at the Last Stand after a day of lectures?

86.original: Oh, that does sound lovely. Afternoons with friends spent sipping tea and debating theories.

87.original: ...Still, I wouldn't give up my time with Master Matoya for the world.

88.original: The dank cave I studied in was about as far from the bright, airy halls of academia as one could get. But it was a wondrous, magical childhood nonetheless.

90.original: Oh, never mind me. 'Twas just an idle thought.

96.original: If I was pressed to name our allies in the Forum, Scholarch Montichaigne would certainly be at the top of the list. Hopefully he agrees to aid us with our request.

97.original: Are you sure you wish to part ways with Y'shtola?

98.original: Need to be somewhere? Very well, I will wait for you by the aetheryte.

99.original: Oh, not to worry─I had plenty of reading to keep me occupied while you were busy. Shall we continue?

100.original: Archon Y'shtola wishes a word with me? Then I shall eagerly await her arrival!

101.original: You must be accompanied by Y'shtola and have her at your side in order to proceed with quest objectives.

102.original: Y'shtola has yet to arrive. Be sure she is at your side before attempting to continue.

103.original: Ah, visitors! And quite esteemed ones at that. What may I do for you?

104.original: Pray forgive the intrusion, Scholarch, but we were hoping you might help us secure permission to enter Noumenon's restricted archives.

105.original: Oho! No furtive forays into the stacks this time, eh?

106.original: I applaud this newfound sense of propriety. Yet in all this wide world of comparative serenity, what so compels you to disturb a vault of forbidden wisdom?

107.original: Fascinating. I had no idea such a technique existed.

108.original: I would've been surprised if you had. If my assumption is correct, the research left behind by House Daemir has lain dormant in Sharlayan's archives for many centuries.

109.original: And if you unearth this research, what then? Surely you don't intend to cross over into the void?

110.original: That is, in fact, precisely what we intend.

112.original: To develop a method of traversing the rift, for one, that I might keep my word to a distant friend.

113.original: Sentiment aside, I have journeyed to the end of existence. I have heard, felt, and thought endlessly about the truth of our world and the echo of its future. And yet I want to understand <hex:021A020203>everything<hex:021A020103>─to unravel it all down to its very last secret.

114.original: What scholar worthy of the name wouldn't force open a voidgate or two if a grand revelation was the promised reward?

116.original: An audacious proposal worthy of Master Matoya herself!

117.original: And after hearing the whys and the wherefores, I for one do not believe you would use the knowledge for ill.

118.original: I see no reason not to present your request for the Forum's consideration.

119.original: Although... Your petition would be better received if you also had the support of another well-placed acquaintance.

120.original: Why, Master Fourchenault, of course! He can hardly ignore an earnest request from his dear children's most treasured comrades.

121.original: I was hesitant to approach him directly, but there is no denying that having Master Fourchenault on our side would tip the balance in our favor. Very well. We will pay a visit to the Leveilleur estate and plead our case.

122.original: Ah, one last thing before you go. I would consider it a personal favor if you might share with me the discoveries you make in the void.

123.original: My appetite for knowledge is every bit as insatiable as yours, I'd wager, so if you could see your way to indulging an old man's curiosity...?

124.original: Of course, Scholarch. We will be sure to pass on any revelations.

125.original: The Forum can be a cantankerous beast─one needs a persuasive voice to get it moving in the desired direction.

126.original: Montichaigne seemed optimistic, but I doubt convincing Fourchenault to champion our cause will be as simple as showing up on his doorstep.

127.original: Welcome to the Leveilleur residence. Have you come alone, or should we expect a larger party...?

128.original: You must be accompanied by Y'shtola and have her at your side in order to proceed with quest objectives.

129.original: Ah, <hex:020815E905FF094D69737472657373FF074D617374657203> <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, Mistress Y'shtola, how may I be of service?

130.original: We've come to speak with Master Fourchenault. Is he home, by any chance?

131.original: Yes, the master is in residence. I shall inform him that he has guests.

132.original: Well, well. Ameliance would invite you inside for tea, but I assume this is not a social visit. You have some matter of import to discuss?

133.original: Then pray proceed─you have my full attention.

134.original: Well, I suppose I should praise you for following the proper protocols this time around...

135.original: Scholarch Montichaigne expressed much the same sentiment. I assure you, we'll not attempt to circumvent the Forum's authority again...unless it is absolutely necessary, of course.

137.original: You do understand that the restricted archives are restricted for good reason, yes? If no pressing need exists, then why risk the consequences of employing this forbidden knowledge?

138.original: For a brother who misses his sister. She was his guardian and his friend─a selfless hero who crossed the rift between worlds to save her homeland from horror and suffering.

139.original: But the brother has given up on thoughts of reunion. He spends his efforts elsewhere, watching over a people yet healing from the flames of the Final Days, loyal to his duty while betraying the longing in his heart.

140.original: 'Tis no vital mission, perhaps, reuniting these siblings. But it feels a worthy cause to pursue, all the same.

141.original: As one who feared losing his own loved ones, and spent years in research to prevent it, surely you appreciate how painful such a separation must be.

145.original: Reflections are still very much a mystery to us. Offering to share your experiences in the First should constitute a fair exchange for our cooperation.

146.original: Do not celebrate just yet. The Forum must still be convinced.

147.original: I will add your request to the list of today's deliberations, and deliver the decision to you at the Baldesion Annex.

148.original: Please do come again. We are always glad to receive such close companions of the twins.

149.original: The matter is out of our hands. All that remains is to return to the annex and await word of the Forum's decision.

150.original: So. What did the Forum decide?

151.original: To put it bluntly, Master Matoya has burned some bridges here in Sharlayan─and salted the earth for good measure. When it became clear that her student was the petitioner in question, well, no few members voiced their discontent...

152.original: Then the chamber was reminded─in no uncertain terms, I might add─of the incredible debt we owe to you and your companions.

153.original: That served to silence the grumbles and stiffen a few spines, and it was agreed that allowing you entry to the archives was the least we could do in return.

154.original: That is wonderful news. Thank you both for speaking on our behalf.

155.original: Yes, well... As I am sure you are aware, this permission was not extended lightly. Forbidden knowledge is to be treated with the utmost caution, and there will be repercussions if it is not.

156.original: I wish you well in your endeavor, and bid you good day.

158.original: Uncompromising? Aye, but that very stoicism is exactly what Sharlayan needed to guide it through not one, but two exoduses.

159.original: If I were but five years younger, I'd cast aside my lectern and join you on your adventures in a heartbeat...

160.original: That went rather well, I think.

161.original: As a child, I dreamed up any number of schemes for getting my hands on those forbidden tomes... And now I can simply walk in through the door.

162.original: Our focus will be on finding House Daemir's research notes, of course, but the thought of so much knowledge at my disposal has me feeling a little giddy.
